name: Double Diagonal Spread
summary: A put diagonal below spot and a call diagonal above, with the short legs in the near expiry and the long protective wings further out in time and further out of the money; an iron condor whose wings live in a later cycle.

legs.strike_rule: Long put BELOW the short put by 1-5 points (width set so max loss <= 1.5% of equity per side).
legs.dte_rule: back expiry, 21-45 days beyond the front

legs.strike_rule: Short call by delta 0.20-0.30, delta-symmetric with the short put within 0.07.
Long call ABOVE the short call by the same width as the put side.

max_profit: Net credit received plus the residual value of the two back-month wings once the front shorts expire worthless. The wings' survival is the entire advantage over an iron condor.
max_loss: (Strike width x 100) - net credit on the tested side, at front expiry, provided the wings are never closed before the shorts.
breakevens: Short put strike - (credit + residual wing value)/100 and short call strike + (credit + residual wing value)/100; wider than an iron condor at the same strikes.

greeks.delta: ~0 when the short strikes are delta-symmetric
greeks.gamma: negative, concentrated at the short strikes into front expiry
greeks.vega: slightly positive to neutral - the later-dated wings carry more vega than the front shorts, so unlike a plain iron condor this structure does not get destroyed by a vol spike, and it benefits modestly from one

when_to_use: IV rank 30-60 with a range-bound underlying. The double diagonal is the right choice over an iron condor when (a) back-month IV is cheap relative to front (backwardation), so the wings cost less, and (b) you want protection that survives the front expiry so it can be reused against a second round of short legs. On a $50k account, run it on liquid ETFs only.
typical_dte: short legs 21-45 DTE, long wings 45-90 DTE
entry_rules: Short strikes by delta 0.20-0.30 on each side, symmetric within 0.07 delta.
Long wings 1-5 points beyond each short, symmetric width on both sides.
Long expiry at least 21 days beyond the short expiry, never the reverse.
Total credit >= 20% of the one-sided strike width.
Max loss per side (width x 100 - credit) <= 1.5% of equity.
Short strikes must sit outside 1.0 x the front-month expected move.
LEVEL 3 OK: each short is covered by a same-side long at a protective strike in a LATER expiry. Submit as a single 4-leg mleg; if it must be legged, fill BOTH WINGS FIRST, then sell both shorts.
management_rules: Take profit at 50% of the total credit.
Stop at 2x the credit received, or when either short's |delta| reaches 0.50.
At 21 DTE on the short legs, close or roll any short whose |delta| > 0.35 regardless of P&L.
Roll the tested short away from spot and out in time for a NET CREDIT only, and never into an expiry at or beyond the wings' expiry.
Roll the untested short toward spot to recenter only if doing so keeps |net delta| < 0.20 per unit and the short's delta stays <= 0.30.

After the front shorts are closed, the two wings remain as a long back-month strangle: either sell a new round of shorts against them (the reason to use a diagonal) or close the wings if their combined mark is below 25% of the original wing cost.
exit_rules: Close or roll BOTH short legs by 14:30 ET on their expiration day, unconditionally.
Close either short immediately if its extrinsic <= $0.05/share or |delta| >= 0.90.
Close the short call before the session preceding ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share.
Close any short put whose extrinsic drops below $0.10 (interest-carry exercise risk).
NEVER close a wing while its same-side short is open - that creates a naked short. Wings are sold only after the corresponding short is bought back.
If spot trades beyond a wing strike, close that side's pair as a package.
assignment_risk: Both short front-month legs, though only the tested side matters in practice. Each is covered by a further-out-of-the-money long in a later expiry, so the worst case is a stock position hedged at the wing strike - defined, but with a gap equal to the strike width. Flatten any assigned stock within one session.
buying_power: Alpaca holds the greater one-sided requirement: (width x 100 - credit) on the wider of the two sides, not both, because the underlying cannot finish beyond both short strikes simultaneously. Confirm the reserved amount before scaling.
liquidity_needs: Four legs across two expiries and four strikes: OI >= 300 per leg, penny or nickel quotes, underlying ADV >= 3M shares. SPY, QQQ, IWM, and the largest sector ETFs are the realistic universe.
common_mistakes: Closing a wing before its short leg; rolling a short past the wing's expiry and un-covering the position; setting the wings only one week later than the shorts so they add cost without residual value; assuming the buying-power hold is two-sided; treating it as an iron condor and applying iron-condor vega intuition (this structure is long vega, not short).
zero_dte_notes: Not suitable - two short legs on a share-settled underlying at 0DTE is exactly the exposure the assignment policy exists to prevent.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
also_filed_under: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
